body:
APPROVED BY MYK IN CHAT, 2026-07-26, after his second run of the same discomfort: "erasure breaks the whole model and we have to keep carving out exceptions everywhere. I don't like it." This ticket converts that dislike into an artifact, in two halves — a spec section that names the principle, and a mechanism that enforces its perimeter.

FIRST LINE, NON-NEGOTIABLE: **this does not reopen the erasure level decision.** Myk chose full provable erasure (2026-07-25) and closed it. The section AFFIRMS the promise and organizes its enforcement; any draft that reads as softening has failed P1 before spec-lint sees it.

THE PRINCIPLE the section states: the model's one deep guarantee is monotonicity — claims are the state, append is the only verb, readers are pure functions of the set. Erasure is the single anti-monotone, EXTRA-MODEL operation: the ground can record the ORDER to forget (a tombstone is an ordinary claim) but the forgetting itself is a fact about BYTES, which the model can point at and never contain. Every erasure carve-out shipped to date is that one seam surfacing at another place where bytes and claims meet — which is why the count of exceptions is the count of PLACES, not principles, and why "can this report be false?" has caught every erasure bug this repo has paid for. It is the seam's signature question and the section should crown it as such.

THE SIX RULES the section derives (drafted in chat, 2026-07-26; P1 may refine but starts here):
- R1 VERIFY AT THE BYTES: every erasure-adjacent report is a claim ABOUT the world; unverifiable reads as not-done, never as clean (H9's tri-state; holds(); receipts; graveyard completeness).
- R2 ORDER AND ACT ARE SEPARATE RECORDS: the order is in-model, append-only, unerasable; the act is only ever WITNESSED — a driver's return value is evidence, never proof.
- R3 FAIL CLOSED FEEDING A PURGE: any derivation whose output widens what gets destroyed refuses on unreadable input (T66's withheld plant; the pre-work completeness guard; T99's whole family).
- R4 THE SEAM STOPS AT AUTHORITY BOUNDARIES: forgetting does not travel — peers, and the viewer's page (T79's residency), are notified, never compelled.
- R5 TWO-SIDED RAILS ALWAYS: removal proven AND a named bystander's survival proven, because over-purge is the unrecoverable direction.
- R6 READERS CONFESS ABSENCE: a hole is shown as a hole (as-of annotations, kept/stranded lists), never smoothed over.

THE CENSUS IS PART OF THE DELIVERABLE, DONE, NOT PROPOSED: every existing carve-out in the tree (~14: tombstone-before-purge ordering; unerasable tombstones + forgiveness; tri-state holds(); as-of confessions; resolver memo invalidation; container/pool fan-out with refuse-on-unreachable; the pre-work guard; slate cite-closure exemptions and erase-refuses-a-pinned-Term; heal's withheld plant; federation non-propagation; the page residency confession; two-sided rail discipline) tagged with its rule. A carve-out that fits NO rule is either a bug or the principle is incomplete — either is a finding, and the audit is the point. Cross-link: H7 and H9 cite the section as the principle they are instances of; the section cites them back.

THE MANIFEST — the enforcement half, because Myk's standing shape is mechanism over lore (the book's coverage gate, the rename exemption, "we can't know in advance what will end up in a limited context window"): a SEAM MANIFEST enumerating every module allowed to touch bytes at rest (src/store/*, erase.ts, the purge paths in slate/container/heal). Two teeth, both designed at P1 with their verification named: (a) a diff touching a manifest module mechanically routes the loam-erasure lens — scripts/p5-triage.mjs keys on the manifest instead of its own heuristics; (b) new code reaching byte-destroying APIs (unlink/rm/DELETE/truncate/purge calls) OUTSIDE the manifest fails CI. The detector for (b) is the hard design question — a lexical scan has H10 risk (a list that only knows the names it knows); P1 must state what it can and cannot catch, honestly, in the section itself. The manifest turns "the seam keeps surprising us" into a closed, guarded set: joining it is a reviewed act.

RELATIONS, deliberately NOT edges (a bug family must not queue behind philosophy): T99 (condemned-set derivation) is R3's largest open instance and should cite the section when built; T90 (erase vs concurrent readers) is R1/R6 territory; T44 likewise. T101 (crypto-shredding, authored beside this) is the section's SHRINK-THE-SEAM subsection made concrete.

DELIVERABLE: working spec at .adlc/specs/32-erasure-seam.md — criteria each naming their verification, per the P1 bar — then STOP for Myk. Design-stage: the landing PR is his decision and his merge, and it writes spec/32-erasure-seam.md. Section number §32 claimed here; never renumber. Per the P6 readability rule, the landing arrives SMALL with a review guide: the six rules and the census table are the read; the manifest mechanics ride separately if they push the diff past a comfortable read.
title: §32 The erasure seam — one principle under every carve-out, and a manifest that makes it enforceable (DESIGN-STAGE)
